bull.b: Management's outlook points to substantial, multi-period expansion rather than a single-quarter lift: 2026 revenue is expected near $1 billion, 2027 growth at least 60%, and five-year CAGR above 30%. This supports stronger scale, program visibility, and investment capacity.

Strong operating and free cash flow indicates that reported earnings are supported by cash conversion, giving Lattice resources to fund research, capacity, and debt reduction. Continued cash generation can improve financial flexibility as the company scales its growth initiatives.

bull.t: Product Innovation And AI-enabled Design Tools
bull.b: Lattice Prompt can reduce the time and expertise required to develop FPGA applications, potentially broadening adoption and strengthening the software-supported ecosystem around its devices. Faster customer development cycles may improve design-win conversion and reinforce platform relevance.

bear.b: The sharp decline in net profitability shows that strong revenue growth has not yet translated consistently into durable earnings expansion. If margins remain volatile, Lattice may have less internal funding for product development and reduced resilience when costs or demand fluctuate.

The rapid increase in leverage raises financial risk and reduces flexibility compared with Lattice's previously lightly leveraged position. Higher debt obligations can compete with research, capacity investment, and shareholder-return priorities if operating performance weakens or growth requires more capital.

Supplier cost inflation and expedite fees can pressure gross margins and cash generation even when customer demand is strong. Although management said costs are being passed to customers, incomplete recovery or continued urgency in procurement could limit the durability of near-term profitability gains.
